resources.string: Shows while SnoopGuard is armed. Android requires this notice while the camera service runs.
A selfie is captured each time the phone is unlocked.
Camera permission is required to capture selfies.
Notification permission is needed for the required running notice.
Android shows a camera indicator (green dot) briefly on every capture. This cannot be hidden, and is by design.
Pick photos or videos to encrypt into your vault with the same key as captures. The originals are read, encrypted, and never stored in the clear by this app.
Create your encryption key first (Watch tab → Arm).
Enter your passphrase to decrypt and view captures and imports on this device. The passphrase is used in memory only and is never stored.
No encryption key yet. Set one up on the Watch tab.
Tap an item to decrypt and open it.

SnoopGuard encrypts every capture to a key that lives only on this device as a public (lock-only) half. To view captures you enter the passphrase you choose here, which unlocks the private half in memory. The phone itself can never decrypt a capture.
Save the exported key file and remember your passphrase. You need BOTH to view captures. If you lose either, encrypted captures cannot be recovered — that is the point.
Passphrase must be at least 8 characters.
